```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Vignette code is executed locally (NOT_CRAN=true) but not on CRAN, where
# training would take too long and the CPU fallback could multi-thread.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true"))
```

rltoolsR runs reinforcement learning in R: environments in C++ (from
[RLtools](https://github.com/rl-tools/rl-tools)) or as ggml graphs, neural
networks on the GPU through [ggmlR](https://github.com/Zabis13/ggmlR) (Vulkan)
with a CPU fallback. Training here is kept short, a few seconds per chunk:
enough to show the API, not to learn a good policy.

```{r}
library(rltoolsR)
```

## 1. Environments

`rl_env_names()` lists the built-in environments. An environment has an
observation space, an action space and a step limit.

```{r}
rl_env_names()

env <- rl_env("pendulum", seed = 1)
env$observation_space
env$action_space
env$max_steps
```

`rl_reset()` starts an episode, `rl_step()` takes an action and returns the
next observation, the reward and whether the episode `terminated` (a terminal
state) or was `truncated` (the step limit).

```{r}
obs <- rl_reset(env, seed = 1)
r <- rl_step(env, 0.5)
str(r)
```

`rl_save_state()` / `rl_load_state()` snapshot an environment, e.g. for search
algorithms:

```{r}
s <- rl_save_state(env)
a <- rl_step(env, 1)$obs
rl_load_state(env, s)
b <- rl_step(env, 1)$obs
all.equal(a, b)
```

`rl_vec_env()` steps `n` copies in one call and returns batched matrices.
Finished copies reset on their own; `final_obs` keeps the last observation of
the finished episode.

```{r}
venv <- rl_vec_env("pendulum", n = 4, seed = 1)
obs <- rl_reset(venv)
dim(obs)
r <- rl_step(venv, c(-1, 0, 0.5, 1))
r$reward
```

Spaces follow Gymnasium: `space_box()`, `space_discrete()`,
`space_multi_discrete()`, `space_multi_binary()`, `space_dict()`.

```{r}
space_size(space_dict(pos = space_box(-1, 1, shape = 2), cell = space_discrete(9)))
```

## 2. Train PPO on Pendulum

`rl_ppo()` describes the algorithm, `rl_train()` runs it for a budget of
environment steps. Continuous actions use a Gaussian policy; observations and
rewards are normalized by default.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
env <- rl_vec_env("pendulum", n = 8, seed = 1)
algo <- rl_ppo(n_steps = 128, epochs = 4, minibatch = 256, gamma = 0.9)
model <- rl_train(env, algo, total_steps = 8 * 128 * 4, device = "cpu",
                  verbose = FALSE)
tail(model$history, 3)
```

`model$history` has one row per iteration: steps, finished episodes and the
losses of the update.

## 3. Evaluate

`rl_evaluate()` runs whole episodes on a separate environment and returns the
mean and standard deviation of the return and the episode length. Episode `i`
starts from seed `seed + i - 1`, so every evaluation sees the same initial
states, whatever `n_envs` is.

```{r}
res <- rl_evaluate(model, "pendulum", n_episodes = 8)
res
head(attr(res, "episodes"))
```

With `greedy = FALSE` the actions are sampled. Each episode then has its own
RNG stream, so the result still does not depend on `n_envs`, and the caller's
RNG is left as it was.

```{r}
rl_evaluate(model, "pendulum", n_episodes = 8, greedy = FALSE)
```

## 4. Act, save and load

`rl_act()` picks actions for a batch of observations (one row each).

```{r}
obs <- rl_reset(rl_vec_env("pendulum", n = 2, seed = 5))
rl_act(model, obs)
```

`rl_save_model()` keeps the weights and the metadata needed to rebuild the
network; `rl_load_model()` places it on any device. A model trained on the GPU
runs on the CPU and back.

```{r}
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
rl_save_model(model, f)
m2 <- rl_load_model(f, device = "cpu")
all.equal(rl_act(m2, obs), rl_act(model, obs))
```

## 5. Tic-tac-toe: discrete actions and self-play

`rl_gpu_env("tictactoe", n)` plays `n` games at once as a ggml graph. With
`opponent = "self"` the policy plays both sides; `rl_legal_actions()` gives the
mask of free cells, which PPO applies before choosing a move.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
ttt <- rl_gpu_env("tictactoe", n = 64, opponent = "self", device = "cpu")
m <- rl_ppo_train(ttt, iterations = 20, minibatch = 576, device = "cpu",
                  verbose = FALSE)
rl_ppo_eval_tictactoe(m, n = 200)
```

`rl_ppo_eval_tictactoe()` plays as X against a random opponent and reports the
fractions of wins, draws and losses. To play against the model in the console:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
rl_play_tictactoe(m, human = "O")
```
